verdict.label: apparent_contradiction
verdict.rationale: Both abstracts report a within-group change in LDL-cholesterol from baseline after a dietary intervention, so the outcome and contrast type are comparable. Side a reports that LDL-cholesterol significantly decreased after three weeks of a high-carbohydrate/low-fat diet in physically active, normal-weight adults (97.9 to 78.2 mg/dL; p = 0.02), while side b reports a significant within-group increase in LDL-C (+9.9%, P = 4.9 × 10⁻⁵) after 1 year of a continuous care intervention including nutritional ketosis via sustained carbohydrate restriction. The directions are genuinely opposite. The abstracts support concrete contextual differences that could explain this: side a studied healthy, physically active adults (BMI 22.1 ± 2.2) over three weeks, whereas side b studied adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity (BMI 40.4 (8.8)) over one year under a continuous care model, and the diets sit at opposite ends of the carbohydrate spectrum (high-carbohydrate/low-fat vs. sustained carbohydrate restriction with nutritional ketosis). These source-supported differences in population, intervention and duration make apparent_contradiction more appropriate than contradictory.

source_evidence.quote: Total cholesterol and LDL-cholesterol significantly decreased after the HC diet (97.9 ± 33.6 mg/dL at baseline to 78.2 ± 23.5 mg/dL; p = 0.02)
Twenty-four physically active adults (14 females, age 25.8 ± 3.7 years, body mass index 22.1 ± 2.2 kg/m2), of which six participants served as a control group, were enrolled in the study.

Intention-to-treat analysis (% change) revealed the following at 1-year: total LDL-particles (LDL-P) (- 4.9%, P = 0.02), small LDL-P (- 20.8%, P = 1.2 × 10-12), LDL-P size (+ 1.1%, P = 6.0 × 10-10), ApoB (- 1.6%, P = 0.37), ApoA1 (+ 9.8%, P < 10-16), ApoB/ApoA1 ratio (- 9.5%, P = 1.9 × 10-7), triglyceride/HDL-C ratio (- 29.1%, P < 10-16), large VLDL-P (- 38.9%, P = 4.2 × 10-15), and LDL-C (+ 9.9%, P = 4.9 × 10-5).
The CCI group consisted of 262 participants (baseline mean (SD): age 54 (8) year, BMI 40.4 (8.8) kg m-2).

diagnostics.notes: Both ClaimV2 extractions were verified against their sources: side a correctly extracts a significant within-group decrease in LDL-cholesterol after the HC diet (direction '-'), and side b correctly extracts a significant within-group 9.9% increase in LDL-C at 1 year in the CCI group (direction '+'). The p_value.value of 1.0 on side b is a minor formatting artifact; the reported_text 'P = 4.9 × 10-5' and the target are correct, so it is nonmaterial. Neither abstract asserts no effect, so not_replicated does not apply. The opposite directions, combined with text-supported differences in population (healthy active adults vs. T2D adults with obesity), intervention (high-carbohydrate/low-fat vs. sustained carbohydrate restriction/nutritional ketosis) and duration (3 weeks vs. 1 year), support apparent_contradiction with factor population.
